items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we have the graph [MATH: y=f(x).] How do we plot the graph of [MATH: y = f(|x|)?]

Content:
First, notice that since [MATH: \left|-x\right| = |x|,] we have that

Content:
[MATH: f(\left|x\right|)=f(\left|-x\right|).]

Content:
Therefore, the values of [MATH: f(|x|)] will be equal for corresponding positive and negative values of [MATH: x.] Moreover, every input is non-negative. Thus, to plot the graph of [MATH: y = f(|x|)] from the graph of [MATH: y=f(x),] we reflect the right half of the graph across the [MATH: y]-axis.

Content:
For example, the graph of [MATH: y=f(x)] is shown below. What is the graph of [MATH: y=f(|x|)?]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/10d7435547fc87616da3b965d495ff7f]

Content:
To get the graph of [MATH: y=f(|x|)] from the graph of [MATH: y=f(x),] we reflect the part of [MATH: y=f(x)] that lies to the right of the [MATH: y]-axis across the [MATH: y]-axis.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5d0f87efc93caf76469c773812e2a66d]

Content:
Watch out: Pay attention to the notation. Although they look similar, [MATH: f(|x|) \neq |f(x)|.] These two functions are defined differently and have different graphs!

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e0a374215db0038a45958ee3e78331ae]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
When we take the absolute value of a function, the positive values of the function remain unchanged, but the absolute value operation removes the minus sign from any negative values.

Content:
As a consequence, to get the graph of [MATH: y = |f(x)|] from the graph of [MATH: y=f(x),]

Content:
- any parts that lie on or above the [MATH: x]-axis will remain unchanged, and
- any parts that lie below the [MATH: x]-axis will be reflected in the [MATH: x]-axis.

Content:
For example, consider the graph of [MATH: y=f(x),] shown below. What is the graph of [MATH: y=|f(x)|?]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/b2d581691b2cc9d953d4b13bef77a98b]

Content:
To get the graph of [MATH: y=|f(x)|] from the graph of [MATH: y=f(x),] we take the part of [MATH: y=f(x)] that lies below the [MATH: x]-axis and reflect it across the [MATH: x]-axis.

Graphic:

Item 5 — Tutorial: Plotting the Absolute Value of the Argument of a Function

Content:
Suppose we have the graph [MATH: y=f(x).] How do we plot the graph of [MATH: y = f(|x|)?]

Content:
First, notice that since [MATH: \left|-x\right| = |x|,] we have that

Content:
[MATH: f(\left|x\right|)=f(\left|-x\right|).]

Content:
Therefore, the values of [MATH: f(|x|)] will be equal for corresponding positive and negative values of [MATH: x.] Moreover, every input is non-negative. Thus, to plot the graph of [MATH: y = f(|x|)] from the graph of [MATH: y=f(x),] we reflect the right half of the graph across the [MATH: y]-axis.

Content:
For example, the graph of [MATH: y=f(x)] is shown below. What is the graph of [MATH: y=f(|x|)?]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5d0f87efc93caf76469c773812e2a66d]
